title: Rightly Handling the Word
definition: Rightly Handling the Word means treating Scripture faithfully, carefully, and truthfully so its meaning is not distorted.
summary: Rightly Handling the Word means treating Scripture faithfully, carefully, and truthfully so its meaning is not distorted.
christFocus: Jesus handled Scripture with perfect faithfulness, and those who teach or study His Word must honor Him by refusing to twist what God has spoken.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Rightly handling the Word means seeking the truth of Scripture rather than using Scripture to support personal agendas. It requires humility, context, careful interpretation, and a desire to please God more than impress people.

The Bible can be mishandled by exaggeration, careless proof-texting, ignoring context, avoiding hard truths, or using truth without love. Faithful handling protects both the message and the people who hear it.

Christ is honored when Scripture is handled faithfully. The goal is not to sound clever or win arguments, but to make God’s Word clear so people can know Christ, trust Him, and obey Him.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People can be deeply wounded when Scripture is misused. Rightly handling the Word matters because God’s truth should not be used to control, shame, manipulate, or confuse those Christ calls to Himself.

This doctrine also warns teachers and leaders. The more influence someone has with Scripture, the more carefully they must handle it before God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Handle Scripture with prayer, humility, and care. If you teach, preach, post, counsel, or encourage with the Bible, slow down enough to honor the text, point people to Christ, and avoid placing your own meaning on God’s Word.
